title: Release audit: The suite runtime regressed past the bound the release established. Task 2026112
summary: Bring the suite back under the documented bound (or raise the bound consistently in README/acceptance and confirm the audit's timeout), then record a passing run of the full suite within that bound. Do not state 'under 120 seconds' while the final suite takes 163 s.
requirements: No project documentation states a suite completion time, duration or runtime bound.
The guidance on running the suite still tells the reader that the single documented command runs the whole suite, with nothing configured or selected that leaves a part of it out.

That guidance still tells the reader that the installer situations are covered, that they perform a real installation into a throwaway home location and use a real detected login shell, and that a run from a source checkout needs nothing beyond the Python standard library and no network access.
Every statement the project makes about how to run its suite and about what such a run covers is true of the project as it stands.
The documented client commands, options, output form, session behaviour and the installer's install, update and uninstall behaviour are unchanged.
All project documentation is written in English.
acceptance: Review of the project's documentation finds no statement of a suite completion time, duration or runtime bound anywhere.

Review finds every remaining statement about how to run the suite and about the coverage of such a run consistent with what the project actually does.

constraints: Documentation states behaviour and contracts, never timings, runtime bounds or durations; a divergence is fixed by removing the detail, not by changing code or tuning a limit.
Documentation is text and is verified by review; no automated check that inspects a documentation document may be added, and this change carries review-only verification.
The release audit's whole-suite budget is owned outside this repository and is not raised here.

result.summary: Documentation-only change that removes the volatile suite runtime figure from the project's documentation while keeping the guidance about how the suite is run and what a run covers behaviourally accurate. README.md `## Tests` now states that a run from a source checkout needs only the Python standard library and no network access, that the single documented command (`python -m unittest discover -s tests`) runs the whole suite with no environment variable, marker or default option leaving a test out, and that the installer situations are covered — a real installation through pip into a temporary home directory with a real detected login shell. The sentence promising the run completes in under 120 seconds (about two minutes) and the following budget claim were deleted; nothing else in the install, options, commands, output, active-project or timeout guidance changed. CHANGELOG.md was edited so the existing Unreleased entry no longer quotes the release audit's two-minute suite bound nor claims the README states a runtime bound, and it gained an entry recording the removal of the runtime figure from the documentation. No product code, installer, client behaviour or test was changed and no automated documentation check was added. Verified by reading the documentation and by running the full suite (`python -m unittest discover -s tests`, 218 tests, all pass) plus the documentation guard test module (34 tests, all pass) to confirm the retained coverage and installer statements still match the project.
assumptions: The README's client `--timeout` default (600 seconds) and the installer's bounded fresh-shell check stay as documented, because they describe product behaviour rather than the suite's completion time.

The Unreleased CHANGELOG entry from the earlier suite-speed task was reworded instead of deleted, so the history still records the harness sharing and the test-configured bound without quoting a suite runtime or a budget.
The documentation task needs no new test; verification is review of the text plus the existing suite run, per the repository rule that documentation is verified by review.

review.summary: The attributed change is a documentation-only edit: README's `## Tests` section loses the 'under 120 seconds (about two minutes)' completion-time/budget sentence while keeping every coverage statement the requirements demand (one command runs the whole suite with no environment variable, marker or default option leaving a test out; the installer scenarios run the real `install.sh` with a real install through `pip` into a temporary home directory and a real detected login shell), and it adds the missing 'and no network access' clause next to the standard-library-only statement, so the guidance now matches FR-3. The CHANGELOG entry that previously recorded the two-minute release-audit bound and the concrete one-second limit was rewritten to describe the speed-up without any figure, and a new entry records the removal of the runtime claim; the removal is done by deleting the detail rather than by tuning code or a limit, exactly as the rule requires. Client commands, options, output form, session behaviour and the installer's install/update/uninstall text are untouched, all text is English, no test was added, weakened or deleted, and no timing, duration or runtime bound remains in the reviewed documentation (README.md, CHANGELOG.md). Verification is review-only and QA was skipped, which is the correct handling for a documentation task.
